data.body:
CI on patchset 1 (Gerrit 1931) failed with 2 real breakages — BOTH caused by the split, both root-caused, neither flaky. Fixed in patchset 2.

FAILURE 1 (the 1916 lesson again, and I missed it): tests/interfaces/contracts/test_bridge_vocabulary_stale_heldout.py::test_no_uncategorized_live_old_spelling. That test holds a path-keyed registry INSIDE A TEST FILE (_COMPATIBILITY_FILES / _WHOLE_FILE_ALLOWLIST) and bans the retired CLI command spellings /(bridge-fsck|bridge-probe|jira-onboard)/ in any tracked file not on the list. My new module's docstring cited ADR 0070 by its slug, which contains the retired command name, so the new file became an offender at line 15. Fixed by rewording to plain 'ADR 0070' — NOT by adding the file to the allowlist, since the new module has no compatibility obligation, it just had bad prose.

FAILURE 2 (a genuine behaviour change — the important one): tests/interfaces/facades/test_bridge_vocabulary_heldout.py::test_setup_final_validation_preserves_the_persisted_settings_overlay. That test does monkeypatch.setattr(config, 'repo_root', lambda *_a: root) — patching repo_root AS A MODULE ATTRIBUTE ON rebar.config — then drives 'bridge setup' and asserts rebar.toml lands in the tmp root. While write_jira_config lived in config.py it looked repo_root up in config's namespace at CALL time, so the patch reached it. After the move it bound rebar._config_sources.repo_root at import time in the new module, ignored the patch, and wrote outside the intended root.

My pre-push analysis checked monkeypatching of the MOVED symbols but not of the symbols the moved code CALLS. That is the generalisable lesson: a move breaks late binding for every name the moved code references through its old module namespace, not just for the moved names themselves.

Fix: write_jira_config now resolves repo_root, _discover_project_config and _parse_toml through the composition root (a function-local 'from rebar import config as _config', function-local because config.py imports this module at its top to re-export the write path). That restores the exact late binding the code had before the move, and matches the rule compose_config/mcp_gate state — a below-seam module RECEIVES composition rather than re-deriving it.

Also correcting my own process error: for patchset 1 I ran only tests/unit + tests/golden locally, but CI runs the whole tree (pytest -m 'not integration and not external'). Both failures live in tests/interfaces, which I never ran. Patchset 2 is validated against the full CI-equivalent suite.

config.py 658 LOC (unchanged), _config_writer.py 196 LOC. make lint 0, make typecheck 0.
